overview: Penlee House is Penzance’s art gallery and museum, in an elegant Victorian house set in its own park a short walk from the town centre. It’s known above all for its paintings by the Newlyn School, the artists who painted everyday life in the fishing villages of west Cornwall in the late 1800s.
It’s a calm, rewarding hour or two, and a natural rainy-day stop if you’re based around Penzance or Newlyn.

expect.title: Newlyn School paintings
expect.text: Works by Stanhope and Elizabeth Forbes, Walter Langley, Norman Garstin and others, including Garstin’s ‘The Rain It Raineth Every Day’.

expect.title: The house and park
expect.text: The house was built in 1865 for a local family and the park around it is now a public space.

expect.title: Local history
expect.text: Collections that grew out of Penzance’s old natural history society.

goodToKnow.label: Before you go
goodToKnow.text: Check the website for opening times and current exhibitions.

week.text: An easy indoor stop in Penzance. Pair it with a stroll through Morrab Gardens next door and along the promenade.

pairWith.why: the fishing port that inspired the artists

tips: Walk on to Newlyn afterwards to see where many of the paintings were made.
